key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% versus bare SA516 steel, delivering the best oxidation resistance among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: This coating could improve the high-temperature oxidation protection of SA516 boiler steel through a dense protective oxide layer, reduced porosity, and increased microhardness.
method: Applied Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterized phases and microstructure using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Laboratory testing linked the best coating performance to protective Cr2O3, TiO2, NiTiO4, and NiO phases, while bare steel showed severe oxide spalling and cracking.
watch_item: Results cover 50 laboratory cycles in air; durability under longer exposure and actual boiler atmospheres remains to be established.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
